Analysis of journal 2470: lines are DR 5500 1827.35; CR 2100 913.67; CR 1200 913.68. Total DR = 1827.35, total CR = 1827.35. The journal balances, so the entry itself is internally consistent.

The finding is that the journal is dated and posted outside its period (period 2, closed 20240305), with POST_DT 20240326 falling after the period end. The fix convention is to reverse the original and, if the expense belongs in the open period, repost it in an open period. The finding is a closed-period posting, not a wrong amount, so the correction should move the net effect out of the closed period into an open period without changing the amounts or accounts.

Open periods available: 11 (20241101-20241130) and 12 (20241201-20241231). The original posting date (March 2024) doesn't fall in either open period, so I can't repost it to its original date. The minimal approach is a reversing journal in an open period that zeroes the original effect, plus the reposting in an open period. However, reposting in Nov/Dec would change the period of the expense, which is a business decision. The conservative correction is a reversal in period 11 that nets the original out of the GL, with the reposting left to the accountant's judgment. Since the instruction is to keep the correction as small as the finding allows, I'll propose the reversal only, with the same accounts and amounts reversed, referencing 2470.

Reversal lines (posted to period 11):
- CR 5500 1827.35
- DR 2100 913.67
- DR 1200 913.68

This balances (DR 1827.35 = CR 1827.35) and no invoice status changes.

Since posted rows cannot be edited and no open period falls in March 2024, this correction reverses the full effect of 2470 in the only open period that fits (period 11, 20241101-20241130), using the same accounts and amounts with debits and credits swapped. Net effect of 2470 plus the reversal is zero. Whether the expense should be reposted in an open period (e.g., 11 or 12) is left to the accountant, since that is a business-period decision. No invoice status changes, as this is not a duplicate-invoice finding. Journal 2469 is covered by a separate finding.
